data.gender_notes: Aadab is used as a unisex name in islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From Arabic adab (أدب) 'refinement, good manners, etiquette', whose plural is ādāb (آداب). In Islamic usage adab denotes the prescribed code of courteous and respectful conduct. Used as a given name, chiefly for girls, in Urdu-speaking communities. Aadab therefore means “Manners; etiquette; refinement; good conduct”. Arabic adab 'refinement, etiquette' (plural ādāb); a recognised Islamic concept of proper conduct.
data.spiritual_meaning: Aadab expresses “Respect, Courtesy, Honor”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.

faq.q: What is adab in Islamic usage?
faq.a: Adab (أدب) is the Arabic term for refined manners and proper conduct - courtesy, respect and appropriateness in daily life. Its plural ādāb (آداب) is the form used as the name Aadab.

faq.q: What does the name Aadab mean?
faq.a: Aadab means “Manners; etiquette; refinement; good conduct”.

faq.q: Where does the name Aadab come from?
What is the linguistic root of Aadab?
faq.a: The root of Aadab is أ-د-ب (ʾ-d-b).

faq.q: How is Aadab written in Arabic script?
faq.a: Aadab is written آداب in Arabic script.

faq.q: Is Aadab a boy's or a girl's name?
faq.a: Aadab is used as a female name.

faq.q: Does Aadab appear in the Qur'an?
faq.a: No. Aadab is not a Qur'anic name; it is used in Muslim naming tradition.

faq.q: Is the meaning of Aadab verified?
faq.a: Yes — the meaning “Manners; etiquette; refinement; good conduct” is established by Arabic adab 'refinement, etiquette' (plural ādāb); a recognised Islamic concept of proper conduct..
